title: api-config-design-scratchpad-anya
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a working sketch for a unified API config schema that can be used by Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes. This is a scratchpad: rough ideas, tradeoffs, and questions to drive a short PRD.

High level goals:
- Single JSON/YAML shape that expresses: routing rules, model preferences, quantization/profile hints, caching policy, batching hints, and fallback chains.
- Backwards-compatible defaults for existing simple route configs.
- Explicit places for operator controls (SLOs, cost caps) vs. developer hints.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Serving runtime must be able to interpret minimal config quickly (startup path).
- Control plane will synthesize advanced policies (can expand to additional fields later).
- Config should be usable in-hosted API and serializable into Dedicated/Private bootstrap files.

Quick sketch: top-level fields (minimal):
- id (string) 
- route (string)  // API route or logical feature name
- model (string or list) // preferred model then fallbacks
- policy (string: "latency" | "cost" | "balanced")
- constraints: { token_limit, time_budget_ms, cost_limit }  <-- NOTE: represent as flat key names instead of nested obj for Drive JSON rules (but runtime will accept nested in implementation)
- pooling: { batching_enabled: bool, max_batch_size, batch_window_ms }
- caching: { prefix_cache: bool, kv_ttl_ms, keyed_by }
- quantization_hint: ["int8", "int4", "fp16", "none"]
- routing: [region/capacity-tier mappings]
- rollouts: { percent, canary }

(Above is a mental model; below is a pragmatic flattened example I want in the schema we store in the control plane)

Flat example record (string keys only - proto-friendly):
- id: api-recommendations-v1
- route: /v1/recommend
- primary_model: redwood/gptx-std-13b
- fallback_models: redwood/gptx-std-6b, open/fast-3b
- policy: latency
- token_limit: 1024
- time_budget_ms: 1200
- cost_limit_usd_per_1000: 0.25
- batching_enabled: true
- max_batch_size: 16
- batch_window_ms: 10
- prefix_cache_enabled: true
- prefix_cache_ttl_ms: 600000
- cache_keyed_by: user_id
- quant_hint: int8
- region_priority: us-west-2,us-east-1
- capacity_tier: reserved
- rollout_percent: 20
- canary: true

Runtime behavior notes:
- On request, control plane resolves the config -> picks model candidate list -> runtime evaluates model availability (capacity/region) -> applies policy (latency vs cost):
  - if latency: prefer lower-latency variant; if unavailable, fallback immediately to next model
  - if cost: attempt batching window to reduce cost; if batching increases latency beyond time_budget_ms, skip batching

ASCII flow for clarity:
  client --> api-gateway --> config-resolver (control-plane) --> routing-policy --> serving-runtime --> model(p1)
                                                                |                                          |
                                                                --> fallback model(p2)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include explicit "quality_hints" (e.g., ngram_coverage_threshold, sampling_temp_range)? Pros: lets control plane detect degradation; Cons: more complex to author.
- How should rate-limits per-route interact with cost_limit_usd_per_1000? If a route has hard cost cap, do we return 402-like error, or degrade to cheaper model? Need product decision.
- How to express multi-model fusion (rerank scoring + generator)? Maybe allow sub-routes or composite route types. Ex: primary_generator + reranker_model.
- Migration story: existing simple route configs (only model + max_tokens) should map to the new schema automatically. Plan: write migration tool in control plane that flattens old fields into new canonical keys.

Notes from chat with Samir (2026-01-14):
- keep the public SDK surface small: only allow model, policy, and soft_hints by default; advanced keys live in "advanced_config" blob that is opaque to SDK but editable in Console.
- We should add a boolean "auto_fallback_enabled" default true.

Mini API example (pseudo YAML):
---
route: /v1/complete
model: redwood/gptx-std-13b
policy: balanced
token_limit: 2048
time_budget_ms: 800
batching_enabled: true
max_batch_size: 8
canary: false
---

Small UX checklist for console (to iterate):
- quick toggle for policy (latency/cost/balanced)
- visible cost estimate per 1k requests based on token distribution (approx)
- quick preview of fallback chain and per-model latency percentiles

Implementation tasks (rough):
- proto/schema: define canonical keys and flag which are "public" vs "advanced" (PR1)  <-- owner: Anya
- control-plane: resolver that maps route -> effective config and computes cost estimates (PR2)  <-- owner: Samir
- runtime: implement enforcement of time_budget_ms and auto-batching heuristics (PR3)  <-- owner: serving-runtime team
- console: update route editor to show simple/advanced view (PR4)  <-- owner: Jamie

Draft decisions I want to lock before a formal PRD:
- flattened canonical key names (see pragmatic section)
- default policy behavior for cost vs latency (degrade vs fallback)
- whether to expose quant_hint to users or keep it autogen by Optimize engine

Rough notes / scraps:
- "auto_retry_on_oom": true?  If model fails with OOM, attempt next model with smaller context.
- Consider a top-level "compatibility_version" int to handle incremental changes.
- Add "eval_suite_ids" list to attach evaluation prompt-sets to the route for regression monitoring (console and alerting).

End of scratchpad.  Next steps: convert this into a short PRD (1-2 pages) and an RFC for the proto change. Will sync with Jamie + Samir next week to align console UX and migration plan.
